title: unique() validation can race during concurrent submissions
problem: CHT issue #10241 reports duplicate records can pass unique() validation when concurrent SMS/API submissions validate before either write is committed.
humanitarian_relevance: Duplicate maternal or patient records can affect frontline health data quality, but the issue touches concurrency design and should not be approached without maintainer design approval.

evidence.claim: Issue report cites production-observed duplicate LMP registrations and provides request timing logs.
A maintainer pushed back on a global queue proposal as too broad and blocking, leaving design unresolved.
On 2026-09-08, read-only GitHub issue metadata reported OPEN, no assignees, 6 comments, and updatedAt 2026-04-08T08:22:17Z. This does not establish maintainer availability or reproducibility.

code_surface: Likely validation utilities, API record/SMS processing, and transition save path in medic/cht-core; exact minimal surface not established.
proposed_change: Park until maintainers specify desired concurrency semantics; possible paths include scoped in-flight claims, CouchDB-backed lock docs, or gateway/API queuing tradeoffs.
tests: Would require a deterministic concurrent submission regression test with synthetic records and no production data.
environment: Tier 3 isolated environment likely required; issue involves API, CouchDB, timing, and resource-constrained concurrency behavior.
maintainer: A maintainer commented that the best solution was unclear and a global queue was undesirable.
risks: High: concurrency changes can reduce throughput, create deadlocks, affect multi-pod deployments, or change data-consistency semantics.
